title: The distance of the polynomial evaluation code determines the unique error correction upper limit
summary: Evaluating degree < k polynomials at n distinct field elements gives minimum distance n−k+1 and uniquely corrects up to floor((n−k)/2) errors.
applies: Finite field polynomials and sampling with errors
detail: Two different candidates agree on at most k−1 abscissas. Checking candidates counts the number of points of agreement over the entire set of observations.
boundary: Erasure in known error locations has different costs than errors in unknown locations. Generally, 2e+s≤n−k needs to be satisfied, where e is the number of errors and s is the number of erasures.
relevance: Determine whether the existing shards are sufficient to uniquely recover the original polynomial, and how to determine candidate consistency.
